late_strong.interpretation: GLD/SLV leadership would have blocked these losers

mid_weak.interpretation: Gold leadership did not prevent macro losses; cross-asset state needs rates/dollar/sector ETF context or timing/overextension filters

old_thin.interpretation: The profitable old_thin macro trades all occurred under stock pressure plus gold/precious leadership

prior_macro_experiments.exp_20260425_005: static macro improved old_thin but hurt late/mid

change_summary: Added a read-only cross-asset audit script. It reruns the static macro defensive sleeve from exp-20260425-005 and annotates each executed macro trade with 20-day GLD, SLV, SPY, and QQQ returns plus derived states such as gold leadership and precious-metals risk-off. No production trading logic was changed or promoted.

delta_metrics.note: This was an information-source audit, not a strategy promotion test. GLD/SLV state has partial explanatory value but cannot distinguish mid_weak losers from old_thin winners by itself.

hypothesis: If macro alpha requires a better information source, then available cross-asset proxies should at least explain some of the difference between profitable old_thin macro trades and losing late/mid macro trades. Start with already available GLD/SLV versus SPY/QQQ 20-day states before downloading new ETF histories.

market_regime_summary.late_strong: macro sleeve losers occurred when GLD/SLV lagged SPY/QQQ despite stock pressure
market_regime_summary.mid_weak: macro sleeve losers occurred even when GLD led SPY/QQQ, showing gold leadership alone is insufficient
market_regime_summary.old_thin: macro sleeve was profitable in a true stock-pressure plus gold/precious leadership state

next_retry_requires: Do not promote a GLD-only or precious-metals-only macro gate yet; it would still admit the mid_weak losing macro trades
If continuing macro, first add or regenerate snapshots with TLT/IEF, UUP, XLE, XLU, XLP, and XLV to test rates, dollar, energy, and defensive-sector ETF context
A credible next macro experiment should require cross-asset state to distinguish old_thin from mid_weak, not merely block late_strong
If missing ETF history cannot be added, pause macro strategy promotion and treat current cross-asset audit as insufficient evidence
notes: This audit supports the decision to change information source, but also shows that the currently available GLD/SLV proxies are not enough by themselves. The next data task is alpha-enabling, not generic infrastructure: add the missing cross-asset ETF histories so macro state can be tested credibly.
